description: Local performance history — records measurements as the user runs optimizations. The MCP learns from what the user does.

entries.notes: kindi 2B ternary: cached ctypes arg marshalling in cupy shim (15.5us -> 3.3us per launch, 331 launches[path] body 28.1 -> 35.0 tok[path] (+24.5%). device-side still 25ms[path] vs 0.7ms roofline: launch count dominates.

CORRECTION of the 35 tok/s entry above, same engine and card. Re-measured with burst replay + host subtraction (paired events report the host submission span when the host is the bottleneck; sync-per-launch reports the driver round trip): device 1.94 ms, host 3.30 ms, wall 3.55 ms/token, 282 tok/s decode, 1726 tok/s read. Launch count 346 -> 130 by capturing 18 layers as replayable command graphs (no numerical change). Device now runs at 242 GB/s = 39% of the 616 GB/s MEASURED streaming rate (not the 1152 GB/s datasheet figure), i.e. 2.54x off roofline; the earlier '25 ms device' was a measurement artefact inflated ~13x and it hid this. Hot kernel is an LDS table decoder: 41 472 B scratch per block pins one block per CU and it spends 64 shared-loads + 64 bit-ops per 96 bytes decoded. Retracted claim: it was NOT purely launch-bound - the wall is host-shaped, but the device is also 2.54x off its own roofline.

notes: This file is updated by the `record_performance` tool.
Each entry records: arch, workload, tok_per_s, config_hash, git_hash, notes.
The `suggest_optimizations` tool reads this history to recommend next steps.
Date-aware: use kands://status for current time before recording entries.
